matchups.tips: Generally before level 6 he can play out the lane rather decently. You don't have any dashes so he should guarantee his full combo if he hits his W on you. At 6 both of you can trade ults with eachother. This is a trade you are fine with, as his ult has 20 seconds extra over yours, and since you cast it first you get about a 22-23 second window where he has no ult but you do. Once you get to Stridebreaker you can really hard chase him down, and at Plated Steelcaps he cannot escape you unless he dashes over a wall. You start to really lay the hurt on him and demolish him in the 1v1, he just cannot kite out your ult reliably anymore. Experimental Hexplate also ensures you have enough speed to straight up ult him when hitting a max range Q.

Very annoying matchup. She will permanently try to poke you down throughout the lane. When you go to last hit minions try to have your E up as much as possible to reduce any possible damage taken. Her wave clear isn't as good as yours early on so you can look for a cheater recall on the 3rd wave so you are able to safely play that part of the lane. You can basically never ult her as she will always use one of her dashes and escape you. What you actually want to do is just perma clear the wave and look to invade the enemy jungle, possibly take voidgrubs, or get something else on the map. At Ravenous Hydra you can instantly explode a wave and move to fights quickly, and if she tries to stop you she will lose her wave under the tower, and you shouldn't even die to her because a single hydra active in the middle of the wave can heal you 400-500 health instantly.

Horrible matchup. If you use ult she can use shroud and just wait it out. You have to deny her the first 3 minions worth of xp on the first wave. Walk past the wave and if she tries to get the xp you can beat her down, forcing her to lose half her health or so. You have to get to the point where you just straight up ignore her. You fullcear the wave with Ravenous Hydra and move to try and get something else around the map, leaving her stuck under turret. Her burst is also massive, so having an early Hexdrinker can help out a lot. Most of the time you will be better than her in teamfights, but it's basically impossible to get a lead on her in lane by killing her, it's mostly just by having higher cs and map tempo.

You don't want to leash level 1. Typically you want to get to the middle brush and fight him for wave control. You out 1v1 him hard level 1 if you don't leash, as you can start chaining axes, forcing him to burn flash or die. It can be hard to chase him down because of his E, but if he ever swings into your melee range you can beat him down hard, even if you are as low as 20% health. Your W shield combined with high damage can ensure you come out on top and catch him off guard. Once you get Plated Steelcaps and Stridebreaker he is always forced to use his E to distance himself from you or he dies on the spot. Before going for a fight with him always wait out his swing and then go for the fight.
Not much to say here, you just destroy him in every single way, he can't even push you under turret because of your ultimate.
You anihilate him in the 1v1, and he can never walk up to the wave.

She has very bad wave clear pre 6, so try to abuse that window as much as possible. You won't get in range to kill her, and she will hard poke you even before 6, but you can push out waves quickly. Ideally you are looking to get off a cheater recall on the 3rd/ 4th wave. Her wall destroys you. It can ensure you never get in range to kill anyone is used properly, it is the ability that makes the matchup absolutely hell. If she uses it wrong, then you can turn and kill her instantly. Your best bet is to just get to Ravenous Hydra as soon as possible, perma clear waves and then look to get stuff around the map. In teamfights the wall once again provides a very good peel tool for herself and her team. If you don't wait her to use it then you can get anihilated. Split pushing is no better either, as she can just throw her ult on the wave and never allow you to hit the turret.
You anihilate her after 6. She can't stun you up and her burst isn't threatening enough, especially once you get to Hexdrinker.
Just watch out for Crescendum (white weapon) and that's about it. He cannot peel you off him and you can anihilate him.
One of the easiest Matchups for Olaf. Her entire gimmick is that she has a permanent slow and can kite well, but you are immune to it in your ultimate, so you just bypass her entire kit.
It's not a bad matchup, the thing is that he can always use his w to fly away when you use your ultimate since you have no hard cc to stop it. If you force it out first then he's easy pickings.

You cannot get pushed back by his ult if your ult is active. That being said, he has his E dash to distance himself from you. Good Azir players will not wait for you to get into melee range so they will use E before you get close to them. Your best bet is to perma clear the waves and look to take stuff around the map. If you sit on lane he will giga poke you constantly and make it very hard to farm without losing a ton of health.

If he roams just take all his plates and turret. The only thing he can do vs you is ult himself or his team. Doing that means your ult will run out by the time they are out of the stasis, but that's literally it, nothing else he can do.

You out 1v1 her early on pretty well. In the hyper late game she has a low cooldown on her dashes and can kite out your ult, but that only happens super late. Before that it's very hard for her to fight you.
Keep in mind that his ult breaks your W shield, so let him ult first and then use W.
After Hexdrinker his burst is a lot less threatening to you and you can run him down well.
His shield can block your Q, denying access to the backline, but that's it really.
She can never W you after level 6 or she just straight up dies. She cannot peel you off her after that. Even if she hits her ult, you just pop your ult as well and kill her.
Really annoying poke due to her long range, but it's managable. If you can tag her with a Q you can run her down once you get Plated Steelcaps and Stridebreaker

She's going to look for very short trades into you, usually when she has her passive up. You can generally bully her in lane decently well, but it can be hard to get kills on her due to her E. She can hold onto it and use it to escape rather easily. You have no hard cc so the only way you can stop that is by being in her melee range and blocking her hookshot. Her gank setup is quite good as well, but most of the time you are actually fine with ganks. Olaf can turn ganks rather well. Sometimes it can give them more confidence if the jungler comes to gank, only for you to turn it and get a double kill. Later on is when the issues start to happen. First off, he ultimate. It can easily block you access to the backline, forcing you to instantly hit her so she steps out of her own ult and lets you go to who your priority target actually is. And then there's her short trading. Early on it's not bad. Once you get Ravenous Hydra you win them very hard, even at Vampiric Scepter you can heal off a ton of the damage she deals. But once she gets to around 2 items, you cannot shrug off her Q2 damage. She will start to deal a ton of damage, and if she just hookshots away after using Q2 on you, you will never catch up to her. This is where Sundered Sky makes it a lot better for you. If you have that, you can actually almost always go even in trades, or even win some of them. You really need Sundered Sky second here. Late game, she outscales you pretty hard. She's very mobile and deals a ton of damage. You can play the role of a peeler, defending your backline, sitting back until she jumps, and then you go with everything on her.

Not as horrible of a matchup as you'd expect. After level 6 you can pop your ultimate and straight up kill her, even if she lands her Q every time and spams her E, you just hard statcheck her in melee. The issue is if she has Phase Rush. If she does, you actually need to force her to proc it before an all in, or else you risk dying because she will outrun your ult. Once she gets Zhonya's Hourglass it becomes quite hard, but she won't take it until 3rd item at the earliest most of the time, so you have a very good window to abuse her. It's also worth noting that her W does not stop you from casting your E. Even though in Olaf's E animation he jumps it is not an ability that is considered a jump, so the grounding does not affect it.
You destroy him in and out of lane after 6. If you tag him with a Q and he's not close to turret he just straight up dies from full health.
Nothing much to say here, just force his W out and he's ready to be all inned.

One of my favourite matchups to play from the side of Olaf. It's very skill expressive on both sides. Olaf has the upper hand early on, but Darius generally beats him more later on. Levels 1-5 can go either way. It all comes down to which player spaces better and abuses their all in ranges more. From level 6 there is a shift in power towards Olaf. Whenever you pop your ultimate to go for him, he has 2 choices. Either Darius burns Flash/Ghost to get away, or he dies. If you fought earlier on and he has no Ghost up you can most likely hard run him down from full health. He cannot E you and he cannot get a Q heal or bleed stack. As long as your ultimate is on you should be able to win it. That being said, the later the game goes the worse it gets for Olaf. For one, if Darius managed to stack up his passive to 5 and drops his ultimate on you, you can actually lose it. You need to abuse the fact that it takes him longer to fully stack his passive and that his E has no effect on you. Usually Darius will go Dead Man's Plate as his second item. By that point he can kite you well, which is why you need Stridebreaker and Experimental Hexplate. This way you can actually keep up with him and not let your ultimate fall off, even though not having Ravenous Hydra overall lowers your 1v1 power. Sterak's Gage as a third item is also a very good option. Darius just has to stack up and then drop his ultimate, and he can win without needing his Q or E, so having a mega shield that eats his entire ultimate and then some is very important. After level 16 is becomes Darius sides by quite a bit. Sure, you can still look for the 1v1, but he will be better in teamfights over you. If you charge in to kill a priority target you might just give him a reset and he will mop up everyone. You need to look to take him out quick and deny him the resets.
You destroy her at every stage of the game.

Boring lane, not a whole lot to it. None of your spells interact with his passive, which is not a bad thing as it means you don't care if his passive is up or not when going in for an all in. You can set up a freeze and force him to just use Q to farm and nothing else. If he actually gets to lane game it's annoying as he has way too much health for you to just shred him down quickly. Around level 11 is when he becomes a lot tougher to kill, and at 16 he is incredibly tanky. Your best bet is to just striahgt up ignore him and rush his backline and explode them. Unless he has Titanic Hydra his damage is lacking, only dealing decent damage with auto+E and that's if he can proc Heartsteel on a target.
You can beat him whenever you want. If he has ignite respect him until level 6, then pop your ultimate and kill him.
Nothing special here, be mindful of his third hit and where he places his W. He doesn't have enough dmg to threaten you. You can also just freeze and make it impossible for him to last hit.
She can't ever beat you, simple as that.
Free lane, not much to it.
Can be annoying but overall easy. If his E is down he dies most of the time.
Even though you can't stop his drain he cannot fear you, nor can he silence you and you hard outdps him in a full all out fight.

Quite a tough matchup. It's kind of a skilled matchup until Ravenous Hydra for the both of you. After the first item it can become Fiora sided. Her dash cooldown becomes low and she can outrun your ult every time. She can use her ultimate for movement speed and then Q away. Once your ult is down she can go back and kill you. You need to try and abuse her early on as much as possible. It becomes really annoying once she hits 2 items. Having Sundered Sky makes short trades sting a little less later on and it allows you to have good sustain, but you really need to outplay her early on.

He can't even threaten you before 6. You can just push him in and never take a bad trade. At 6 a fully charged ult might kill you, but he needs to use every spell to do so, and if he doesn't kill, he flat out dies.
He cannot escape from you in melee range because his E shoots him backwards by a bit. You destroy him.

This can be an annoying matchup. Level 1 he can start E and have a keg at his feet. He can be pretty safe with it and there's not a whole lot you can do about it. If he actually starts Q it's best to sit in his Q range and let him spam it. It doesn't deal all that much damage and it makes him run out of mana quickly. Level 6 you can all in decently, but you need to have enough distance to run him down. If you tag him with a Q he can use his W to cleanse the slow, removing the slow and you losing your Approach Velocity speed. The trick in this matchup is to know when you can auto attack a keg and when you need to go for a full all in where the kegs don't matter. You can usually use his level to determine if it's worth to use the auto attack on a keg or not. For example, if he is between levels 7 and 12 he needs to use one of his auto attacks and then a q on a keg to explode it. It could be more worth to let him do that while you go for the full damage on him. There's a chance you do not time your auto attacks properly and you just end up cancelling them as the barrel goes off. You can use auto+w to get 2 auto attacks in quickly, and that way you can destroy it and that is the most reliable one. After level 13 it could be worth to weave in that 1 auto attack on the keg. Because of how fast it ticks down the Gangplank might panic and hard focus on making sure the barrel goes off and does damage. If you see him overfocused on the kegs, ignore them and just go fully into him. It becomes a battle of burst and you need to win it, which is why I think Death's Dance second is a good choice here, as it allows you to have the bleed damage ticking you down instead of all at once, meaning you have more time to kill him before he kills you.

It can actually be fine to play out in lane. The issue is you are never killing him if he has Phase Rush. His Q cleanses your slow, meaning you also lose the Approach Velocity speed. He is very resistant to dives as well. Even if you try to 2v1 him under tower he can take one of you down as well because of his ultimate. His ult is also the reason as to why the matchup is hard. Olaf loves to fight at lower health because of his passive giving him extra attack speed and lifesteal. The issue is, Garen can just straight up use his ultimate to kill you and never allow you to play from that lower health. If you ever dip below 25% health and he has ult, you die. It's not like Darius where he needs stacks, he just ults you and then you die, so you can basically never go in first because of it. His ult can shut you down by itself. Late game when he has his rank 3 ultimate you can die from close to 50% health. He can also match you very well on the side lane. He can perma clear waves and just not interact with you. He can get to fights quicker as well due to the items he generally builds such as Dead Man's Plate, Force of Nature and other speed items. Your best bet is to set up a freeze early on and at least deny him that farm, or try to hard proxy and rotate to objectives and fights first. Even though he cannot 1v1 you from full health until the hyper late game, he can make it to where it doesn't matter by just clearing waves and maing the both of you go even, which is a win on his end.

It can be very annoying to get a lead on him in lane. He can always just jump away from you and outrun your ultimate. He will also have Fleet Footwork most of the time, meaning he can also use that speed to escape it even better, on top of his W speed. You can kill him if he is pushing into you and he is in Mega Gnar as his jump puts a loss less distance between the two of you. He also cannot use his ultimate or W stun on you because you are immune to them in your ult. Once you get to Stridebreaker it actually becomes a bit more managable and you can more reliably beat him down. At Experimental Hexplate you should have enough speed to stick to him and kill him even with his Mini Gnar jump.

If he has Grasp of the Undying as his keystone you are completely fine and the matchup becomes easy. If he has Phase Rush that's when the issues start to come in. You always need to burn his Phase Rush before you go for an all in, or he will outrun your ultimate. Once his Phase Rush is down yu can beat him down well as he cannot escape without flashing.  Also remember to always stay in front of him so he cannot E away. In teamfights he cannot peel you off anyone no matter what, only try to damage you. If he is playing full ap then his burst can do a lot to you, but with Maw you can eat basically all of it. If he is playing tank he is horribly equipped to deal with you.

He is actually quite strong in melee range due to the way his passive works, and he can gain a lot of distance when he uses his ultimate and E. Fleet Footwork is also a major pain if he has it. That being said, you can out 1v1 him in melee range most of the time. The one thing you actually need to watch out for is his Smokescreen. If you are in it you cannot see anything, meaning you cannot auto attack so you need to get out of it asap. Your E will also cancel if you use it when you see the enemy but then lose vision of them, which can cost you important kills. In the hyper late game his damage and healing goes through the roof, so try not to let the game go there

Level 1 you destroy her, level 2 she can actually fight you well, and from levels 3-5 you can beat her out well, but it comes down to individual skill. At 6 it heavily depends on how both players space out, but it is Olaf favored by a bit. He can just choose when he wants to hard engage a fight. If you do not die early on then you should be okay. If Gwen takes ignite, which most of the time they do, skip the Vampiric Scepter and just go for a Hexdrinker rush, especially if she is taking heavy damage. That way you can all in her and tank through her entire ult. At 2 items you can beat her down really well, you are insanely strong, and the Maw shield will block an insane amount of her burst. In the hyper late it swings pretty hard and she can 1v1 you. If she has Zhonya's Hourglass then you will lose it more often than not because your ult will run out.
You just beat him at all stages, he cannot match you.

You do not want to leash into him. Make sure you get to lane first and do not allow him to set up his turrets for free. Take them out so he needs to place new ones before the minions spawn. The issue with this matchup is that if you ever try to all in he will put down his big turret and look to 1 shot you. You need to wait for at least Hexdrinker. If you do that you can hard all in and look to burst him down quicker than he can burst you down. Once you have completed Maw, you can easily tank through the turrets, as the shield will block around 500 health or more, even as a first item. However, should he rush Zhonya's Hourglass, you will lose the 1v1 again. If you see him having Seeker's Armguard in his inventory, do not finish the Maw, just start building into Ravenous Hydra and then do Maw. After that, look to perma proxy the waves forcing him to sit under tower the whole time. He cannot deny your proxy and you can go do other stuff around the map. His burst will always be massive, so always be mindful of it.

The reason I think Hwei is a hard matchup is simply because of how long his range and waveclear is. You are never killing the guy. He never has to step out of the turret. He can constantly waveclear and farm up without you ever being able to kill him. If you want to dive him you will always trade 1 for 1, and you can never get close to him without your ult up. Like a lot of other matchups, look to proxy and rotate to objectives first or look to get something on the map, like deep vision in the enemy jungle or even taking camps.

One of Olaf's worst matchups in the entire game. You want to go in and use your ultimate to fight it hard, but her burst is twice that of yours and she will shred you much quicker. If she holds onto her E and waits for you to all in, then you basically always die. You can be 5/0 but if she hits her E and then ults, you will probably lose that 1v1. You can ONLY fight her if you have Exhaust up, or else you risk dying instantly. Late game you cannot 1v1 her, even if you have Exhaust up you still might lose. Your best bet is to try and teamfight and get on top of the backline quickly. Illaoi can only ever teamfight if her flash is up. If she doesn't have flash up then it becomes much harder for her to find the right angle to 1 shot enemies.

Level 1 you want to go behind the wave and deny her of the xp from 3 minions. If she tries to get the xp she loses half her hp for free. If she misses her E you can always run her down and win almost every trade. If she hits it, then it can be problematic. You can still win it but a lot less reliably. At level 6 you can beat her, but the issue isn't so much her burst, but the fact that she can dash a lot to a ton of minions. If she starts dashing all over the place your ultimate will run out and that is the actual issue. If you are in a minion wave and Irelia can dash to minions, you need to wait for her to kill every single one and then use your ult or else she can just kite you and then turn to kill you once you lose that power. Do not panic if you start getting low. By the time you are around half her health at least 4 of the 6 minions should be dead, and once all of them die you beat her. If you are struggling with her healing you can rush Bramble Vest or Executioner's Calling if you feel like it.
He cannot kite you at all because of your ult so he can't cheese kill you.
She can't use her Q or ultimate to peel you off her so she dies quickly. If she roams just hard take plates.

He cannot 1v1 you at all. The actual issue with him is that his ult can trap you and not allow you to reach the targets you want. There is a chance that if you engage super quickly and unexpectedly he will also trap one of his allies in the ultimate, forcing him to drop it if that ally has no way of escaping.

Respect his level 1, it is quite strong. What you want to do is Q from range and just slowly farm up until level 3. At level 3 if he jumps on you and burns his Counter Strike too quickly you can kill him. Most of the time he will do Q+auto+W and then back off, and you can do a quick Q+E+auto and even out the trade most of the time. If he tries to continue the trade with his E you can start walking back which forces him to end his E early, and since his dash would still be on cooldown it means you can chase him down for a kill once it's down. At level 6 it can go both ways. If he has Ignite he has a lot of kill pressure on you, but it is managable. He will still look for very short trades, but this time he will also have the third auto attack from his ultimate passive and it hurt quite a bit, but even if you were to lose the trade by quite a bit of health you are still fine in the longrun. The reason being that you want to rush Ravenous Hydra and once you get to Vampiric Scepter you can heal off most of the damage after the short trade is done, and at the full Hydra you will win every single short trade so long as you fight within a minion wave, because the active will heal almost any damage taken in a short trade. When you look to all in Jax, always be mindful of his E. Since you cannot auto attack him your ult will run out. One thing you can do is hold onto your E for when he uses his Counter Strike so you don't have it run out, since Olaf E also extends the ultimate duration. In the hyper late game he will typically beat you because he can get mutiple E procs off, and if he buys Zhonya's Hourglass you really will not win that.

Typically Jayce takes Phase Rush so it will be very hard to catch up to him, so much so that more often than not I take Ravenous Hydra over Stridebreaker, simply because Phase Rush gives champions so much speed with it that into basically any matchup when I see that rune I don't even atempt to get close to them, like ever. He will constantly poke you down from range and you can do very little about it. The one time you can 100% kill him is if his Phase Rush is down and he jumps on you to try and greed an extra trade. With your ult he dies from that. The matchup is actually not that horrible if he doesn't have Phase Rush as you can kill him a lot more, but generally that's not the case. Generally look to go into teamfights more and try to quickly rush down the enemies, Jayce wants to spam poke and weaken everyone before going in to kill, so it's ideal you never allow him to do that and engage at full health.
He can't distance himself properly from you so you just kinda run him over.
You go through her traps and slow so she gets destroyed.

It's actually quite a boring matchup, it's mostly about being patient and not being greedy. The only way he ever kills you is if he pushes you into turret or you allow yourself to get really low. He cannot really force a fight with you, just slowly poking, but the poke is so slow that just having Vampiric Scepter is enough to outheal his Q+auto damage. He can kite your ult decently when he uses his own. His W cooldown resets and he can also save his E dash on top of the initial dash the ultimate provides. If you are in your ultimate and he uses his next to a wall, you do not get taken. Instead, he goes over the wall but you do not. This can end up being both good and bad. It's good because you don't risk going under turret, but it can be bad because this can also be used as a very good escape tool from an all in on your end. At your 3 core items you really start to hurt a lot and can chip his health under turret reliably, forcing him to back off and give you turret damage.

Not a horrible lane, but she can give you somewhat of a tough time due to her own ultimate. She also has decent burst damage early on and she can surprise you with her high damage if she hits her W. Late game she will most likely go for the full ap high burst poke damage. It's very important to not let her get there. You can actually freeze the wave and never let her farm, only through her W, or set up a dive and kill her under turret pretty reliably.

Play safe until your first recall. After that you can start to more reliably fight her. Her movement speed determines her jump range, so if you tag her with your Q then you can reduce how far she can jump. Once you get to Stridebreaker it's basically over for her, she cannot kite you after that. Just be patient the first and second recall, and then you can play it well, but until those 2 recalls it can be painful.

It's quite annoying until level 6. After evel 6 whenever she's halfway up the lane she basically dies, unless she has Phase Rush, at which point the lane becomes much tougher, but they don't take it most of the time.
Even if he hits every single Q on you he gets run over. If you want to be extra safe do Maw of Malmortius second.
You can hard deny him and bully him even turret. Can even look to perma dive him.

Her gimmick is trying to poke you down slowly with short trades and daggers, but you can easily heal up once you get Vampiric Scepter and destroy her. At Ravenous Hydra it's basically pointless for her to try and trade with you. You might lose 5% of your hp while she will most likely lose 30% at least.

You can deny her the first 3 minions worth of xp by walking past the wave and stopping her there. You can also look to push into the turret the 3rd or 4th wave and get a cheater recall off. The wave will bounce back and you can look to hold a freeze. However, here is the issue: unless you can guarantee you get to Kayle and kill her you will break the freeze with any form of fighting. Olaf has to chase down really far and that can break the freeze by walking through some minions and tank some damage, giving the wave a chance to break up the freeze created. At the same time, even if you tag Kayle with Q, she can use her own Q to slow you down and you will not be able to reach her. He also has poor gank setup in this situation because you really want hard cc to lock Kayle down properly, so you rely on the jungler to bail you out. The best thing you can hope for is to try and permanently hold up a freeze, never interacting with Kayle. Even if it seems tempting, she can still escape. Ideally you get to around level 6 while she is just hitting 5, and that can give you a window to set up a dive. This is your only window to beat her. After this, she starts to anihilate you. Once she also hits 6 it becomes hell for you to fight her. If you ult in she can use either her Ghost or her own ultimate and live, and she can mega abuse you while your ult is down. Once she gets to Boots of Swiftness it's over. She can never die, but she can always run you down. You either hard abuse her in the first 5 levels or you get anihilated. And sometimes that's not enough as well because it's up to the jungler to come dive the Kayle early or to just kill her.

Once he gets Rhaast (red form) he can actually beat you well. His dueling power goes up quite well and he can just use his ult to stall out yours and there is nothing you can do about it. You have to hard abuse him before he hits his form, because once he does, it becmes a lot harder to beat him. At 2/3 items he can really take you down and fight you well, and in the hyper late game you will get caved in.

You can never 1v1 him and you are not stronger than him in teamfights. Your best bet is to perma proxy and look to get to the objectives and fights first. In the mid to late game you need to push up side lanes, forcing him to answer you. He is way better in a 5v5 than you are, so at least forcing him on a side lane is better than flipping a 5v5 teamfight where he can blow up your entire team.
As long as you don't stay isolated you are fine. He can also use his ult to stall out yours decently.
Her ult can save some of her teammates, but it can also allow you to get everyone low if there are multiple enemies in the circle and it can provde to be better for you than for her.

Levels 1-5 can go for either one. It heavily depends on how well both sides play. His heal cut is very annoying and can pose a threat to you at all times. You need to hard burst him once he dismounts because if he remounts he will almost always win. Your level 6 is generally stronger than his and if he tries a full out all in you should be on the winning side most of the time. The issue is that he has a lot of pressure until level 6, and at 6 he can trade his ult for yours, and that's better for him, as he can fight you once your ult is down. Once you get to Stridebreaker and Plated Steelcaps that is when it becomes harder for him to beat you. Generally he looks to very short trade into you a few times and then goes for the all in, so with those 2 you can chase him down when he tries to run away with his E. Once you also have Experimental Hexplate that is when the matchup fully swings and you can start beating him down. That being said, do not underestimate his damage, it is still quite high and the heal cut is always a threat to you.
You hard statcheck him in melee range every time.

The reason you don't go Stridebreaker here is because even with it her high mobility and good cs makes it to where you cannot catch up to her even with it,so it's best to focus on healing up in the wave. Ideally you want to get to Ravenous Hydra and perma clear waves, then look for other stuff around the map like invading or taking Voidgrubs.
You both outsustain him and out 1v1 him.
She cannot space you out with her ult or Q stuns, free lane.

She is incredibly quick and even though her ult doesn't affect you, she can more often than not outrun your ultimate duration and then turn on you. If she phas Phase Rush forget about killing her, just perma clear waves with Ravenous Hydra and you're fine.

You can't rly kill her due to her E and ultimate, both of which can mess up your ult and make it to where it falls off. Because of this you shouldn't bother killing her, just perma clear the wave and get something else on the map, like an invade, roam or objective taking.

You have to keep in mind that you will most likely eat his entire ultimate damage as you charge at him, so it's ideal to ensure you stay healthy on the level 6 all in before you go for the kill. Once you get to Stridebreaker the lane is completely over. His only spike is right at level 6, and even there you can run him down.
She cannot cc you so you just destroy her.
Her binding won't stop you so she dies anytime you tag her with Q.

Your Q already shreds armor and since he likes to get a lot of it that's already really good, and then you also have your E which is true damage, meaning it just goes through however much armor he has. If he plays Q max poke Malphite just do Maw of Malmortius second.
He cannot ult you, very easy lane for you.
He cannot knock you back or stall you in any way.

In lane it's not too horrible. You cannot stop his W once he starts it, and his level 6 all in is actually quite strong especially with Ignite, so try to ensure you have Bramble Vest before you hard fight him, or you actually risk losing it.
He can clease your Q slow but that's it, easy lane.
You are immune to her slow so you can always run her down if you tag her with a Q.
Just use your ultimate before he uses his and he cannot steal your stats, nor can he take you in the realm. Every single time he is halfway up the lane and you hit a Q just pop your ult and he dies.
Her Black Shield can prevent you from getting your Q slow off, but that's it really. Easy lane.

It can actually be mildly annoying because all she will do is permanently use her Q to poke you down, but once you get at least Tiamat she gets destroyed. At Ravenous Hydra she can never get you into her lethal range, ever. You can just hold onto the active until she jumps on you and then use it. You will instantly kill every single one of her dogs and heal based off the damage dealt.
Pop ult and run her down once you tag her with Q.

The lane is mostly about wave management. You want to ensure you freeze up and never let him walk up to farm for free. If he has Phase Rush then it could be quite difficult, as if you want to go for an all in you must make sure he does not have it, or you will not kill. Another thing you can do is let the wave push under his turret and constantly E him under turret, chipping his health bit by bit. His healing won't be able to keep up with the constant damage, especially if you also have Executioner's Calling and you manage to proc it each trade. If Nasus does end up having Phase Rush in his runes it could actually be better to max your E first so you can deal a lot of true damage early on and not even have to worry about the mana used. This is in the case if you also cannot hold a freeze on your side for long enough.
He cannot kite you out so he just dies the moment you tag him with a Q.

You can actually kill her, but the issue is her W. If she procs it then she will get a lot of speed and she can also activate it for the clone, and that becomes a mindgame at that point. If you tag her with a Q yu can go for an all in as she cannot trick you with her W. The clone will not be slowed down, but she will, so you can tell wher to do the chase and close in for the kill. Her E and ultimate do not affect you, so should you tag her you can kill.
She just can't punch through you, at all. Once you have Ravenous Hydra you heal off any damage she deals.

You have to be careful of her W as it is basically a Jax Counter Strike, so she can make it to where you cannot auto attack. There' also the fact that she can dash 2 times quickly through her own minions and that can make you drop your ultimate. Other than that, it's a solid lane for you, not super hard, but you need to play around that W and try to burn at least one dash before going in.
Be careful of his levels 1-5, but after 6 he is never winning a single 1v1 into you.
He doesn't have the damage to kill you. At level 1 you can walk in the middle of the wave and tank his snowball a few times and not care. At Ravenous Hydra you can always heal his entire basic combo.
Generally the one who burns his W when it does offer the maximum value loses. You also want to instantly use your ultimate when you start the fight, no waiting at all.
The thing that makes it annoying is that usually she takes Phase Rush so you always need to burn it before going in, but that's literally it. Once it's down and you tag her with Q she dies.
You are immune to his brittle auto attack damage during your ultimate. If he is ever halfway up the lane and you hit a Q he just dies as you can run him over.

You just need to survive until Phage and Cloth Armor. After that you can start to fight him reliably. The issue is he has a ton of poke with him constantly using Q and he has high kill pressure. If you need to give minions, do not greed, just back off and lose a few. If walking up for a minion loses you more than 10% of your health it is bad. As a rule, you can afford to lose a maxium of 4-5% of your health per minion killed, so if you go to kill 3 minions at once it is fine to lose a total of 12-15%, but higher than that can be problematic. Once you get to Stridebreaker and Plated Steelcaps it becomes much easier to 1v1 him. You just have to close the gap quickly with your ultimate and beat him down in melee range. If you want you can also take Sundered Sky second instead of Experimental Hexplate.

Her constant Q poke can be annoying. You cannot just straight up use your ultimate into her if there are minions nearby. She can E one of the minions and then W for the speed and outrun your ult. You need to play it slow, making sure that whenever she goes for a Q you use your own Q+E to win the trade. Once you get Vampiric Scepter you start to win a lot in trades. Even if you were to lose them, the lifesteal ensures you can heal back up nicely. It's just about sustain on both sides, and which one can do the better trades. If you can damage her but then you are allowed to heal minions for free then you win the trade by default, even if she loses 20% health and you lose 50%, you still come out on top as you can hard lifesteal and make the trade even, but she cannot. In teamfights you can just ignore her and rush the priority targets.
He can't get you low once you get Vampiric Scepter, and at Ravenous Hydra it's over.

She cannot ult you to a wall, but she will look to poke a ton. If you want to be extra safe get an early Cloth Armor and then go into Ravenous Hydra. Once you have Ravenous completed the lane is completely done.

Annoying matchup, it can be very hard to hit your Q on her. If she gets Boots of Swiftness it becomes very hard to chase her down for a kill until 2 items. If she has Phase Rush then just rush Ravenous Hydra and forget about ever killing her, just try to hard push her in and not let her roam, if she can't roam she can't really push her lead as hard. She can still bully you, but if she doesn't get kills it's not at bad. Late game she actually beats you in side lane because f her very high speed when she uses he passive so you cannot stick on her reliably. Your best bet is to look for teamfights since you are usually a lot better than her over there.
He cannot charm you or knock you up so you can get to hs carries and ignore him.

Your Q shreds armor and your E has true damage on it so you can actually kill him quite fast. If you want it to be extra funny max E first and watch as his armor is completely uselss. It's not really ideal, but it is funny.

She has insane sustain due to her passive and constantly being able to use it. She has really good sustain. If you find you are not keeping up with your own lifesteal you can take Executioner's Calling and cut a lot of her healing. Her borrowed E can also be annoying as it can make her outrun your ultimate. She isn't super hard to deal with, just very annoying because she can stonewall lane hard and not let you get a reliable lead outside of just having more farm.
Not much to say, she can't pull you with her ult or stun you at all so you can kill anyone she tries to peel.
Her ult doesn't affect you at all so you never need to worry about it.

The way this matchup works is that you win the all in at full health, typically, but if you even dip 5% of your health before you go on that all in, you lose it. You need to be absolutely full health to win the all out brawl because Renekton will typically take Ignite. If he doesn't it's not as needed to be full hp, but if he does, always make sure you are as close to full as possible. You also have to keep in mind that his W can break your shield, so timing is key. Try not to panic and wait for him to use his empowered stun before you use it. You can even use it in the middle of his W stun animation and it will not break it. As long as you didn't W before his first hit then it will not break. His double dash can also be quite annoying, but it is not that bad all things considered, it's pretty managable. Later on it gets a lot better, and as you get to your first and second item you beat him down well and can more than match him in the side lane.

He will constantly look to hard bully you in the early game. Respect his level 1 as he is one of the champions who can challenge Olaf in the early game and win. His general trade pattern is to jump on you with full ferocity, wait for you to use your combo and then him healing it off with his double W, dealing damage while taking none. When he just on you do not panic and do not spam your abilities. Go into an auto attack fight with him as you will win it. You have higher attack speed than he does and you have passive lifesteal as you get lower, so he will be forced to burn his stacks on a spell, and when he does, you can tag him with Q+E and then he would only heal 50% of the damage instead of the full amount. There's also the fact that he has the lane advantage most of the time as he can just weave in and out of brushes very reliably and annoy you big time. Even at level 6 he can jump on minions to distance himself from you or use his own ultimate to escape your all in. Once you get to Sundered Sky he is forced to use spells in trades or he never wins. However, if he also has it then it's back to waiting out until he uses his empowered ability and then using your spells.

She can actually win the level 1 fight if she starts the fight with her Q3. She will have all 3 empowered auto attacks as well and will be able to get a second Q combo in and win it. If you see her do this, do not fight her. Just back off after the Q3 hits you. Before your first recall she can be very annoying when trading. She will just do short trades and back off. Typically she uses Q3+auto+W+auto and then uses E to back off. If you do not hit your Q as she is running away you will lose the trade big time. It's also not a good idea to trade into her. Riven wants to get you low as she has higher initial burst over you, so even if you trade 40% of your health for 60% of hers, you are losing that, especially after level 6. The reason you lose it is because you are in an all in range, but you yourself cannot burst her as fast. Even if she is lower health than you it does not matter when she uses her full combo on you. At full health she can 100-0 you with Ignite a lot of times. You must respect her level 6 spike. Ideally you get to a Cloth Armor and Ruby Crystal and then you can fight the 1v1 as you should be tanky enough to survive her burst. Even if she has a Pickaxe to your 2 components, which costs more gold than then 2 of them combined, the extra tankiness from those items is very good. In the build path you will see double Ruby Crystal, and that's not a mistake. You actually want to have a Cloth armor and 2 Ruby Crystals in your inventory and then start upgrading into the components, as they give you a lot of health and that is what you need. Typically if you have these you will have well over 450 health on riven, as she does not take double scaling health in runes, and sometimes she does not even take the last one as scaling health but instead flat health to spike up his pre 6 even harder, on top of the fact that Olaf has higher base health than her. If you manage to survive this early portion you are good to go. Once you get to your Stridebreaker and Plated Steelcaps it becomes very hard for her to escape, as you now have a second slow when he tries to escape, and at Experimental Hexplate the only way she can outrun you is if she can use her jumps over a wall. In the hyper late game she can 1v1 you unless you take Sterak's Gage and Sundered Sky, then you should be able to beat her out again, but it also becomes much harder to keep up with all her dashes as she keeps building ability haste, constantly reducing her cooldowns.

Very terrible matchup for Olaf. You are forced to take Ghost+Exhaust for him or else he will destroy you in melee range when he overheats, and if you never go for an all in he will just use his Q to constantly poke you and destroy your health bar. You need to go for an all in or you are doomed. If you don't manage to get a lead early he will run you over. Going even with him would be good, but more often than not you just end up losing your entire hp bar just for daring to last hit. Even under turret he can murder your hp bar with his Q, and if he ever hits both harpoons on you, you just straight up die if your exhaust isn't up. Even if you have the full Maw he can shred through it can still beat you down, but if you rush it then it might be too much for him. Unfun matchup, but that's just Rumble in general.

He will typically take Phase Rush so you always need to get it off him before you can go for an all in. He can also trade ults to escape from an all in, but his is quite a bit longer on cooldown than yours so you are mostly fine with that trade. He will mostly just look to just clear waves and not really try to fight with you so it can be hard to take out his Phase Rush and find the kill. He also scales quite hard so try to shut him down in lane as much as possible. You can look to set up a freeze and deny him as much farm as possible. If he tries to farm with just his Q you can tank it because it wouldn't be empowered by his E.
You just outduel her at every stage of the game. The only time you really need to be careful is at level 6, and that's if she has Ignite. If she does not, you can hard all in her.
She cannot stun you in anyway meaning she also won't do any bonus damage from using an auto attack to deal the bonus damage. You beat her and force her to sit under turret the whole game.
She can be annoying if she buys Boots of Swiftness, but it's not bad. She has low mobility in general and if you can tag her with your Q you can look for an all in.
She cannot slow you down in any way when running towards her so you walk over her easily.

Be careful pre level 6 as he can actually put up a good fight and beat you down. After 6 however you start to get the upper hand as it becomes incredibly hard for him to reliably hit you with his W since he cannot stun you. Once thing Sett will often to is trade his ultimate for yours. He can use his ultimate to just distance himself from you since you don't get picked by him as you are cc immune. If he has Ignite he can actually do decently even at 6, and if he angles his ultimate properly you will be forced to use Ghost to get the kill, or else your ultimate drops off and you die. He will constantly use his ultimate to distance himself from you when you pop your own ultimate, so always keep that in mind. In the hyper late game you need to dodge his W or you die, as his true damage will almost 1 shot you if you get hit by it.

You can actually buy a Sweeping Lens level 1 and destroy his boxes. All the champion wants to do is cheese kills by baiting you in when he is low health. All you need to do is sit back, and not do anything really. Just let him sit there with low health. If he doesn't recall, he loses farm as he would have to put a box down at his feet every time he wants to walk up for minions, so then he cannot trap areas around him. If he doesn't do that and tries to use them to bait you, then he is just losing cs for free. You can also buy a control ward and drop it in the middle of the lane and dare him to walk up and take it away. If he does walk up, he will probably kill it, but lose about 70% of his health in that process. If it remains alive, any nearby box is relvealed and you can kill it from a distance. At Ravenous Hydra he never kills you, ever. He simply does not have the damage unless you walk through his entire set of traps, and even then it might not be enough.

Not a super hard lane, the issue with it is that you tend to not be able to get a lead outside of cs. He is probably never going to fight you and just wait for the jungler to come and 2v1. If he has Ignite you probably lose due to the heal cut, but if he has Teleport you should be able to win it. Keep in mind that his W blocks your auto attacks so it's best so save E for when he uses it to extend your ult duration with it since your autos don't do it in that situation. After 6 you want to constantly push him in so he cannot ult safely without losing turret platings. You can also hard freeze the lane and never let him walk up to farm, and if he does end up using his ultimate, you can very quickly break the freeze and punish him, or force him to instantly use his Teleport to get back to lane. If you also happen to have Tiamat when doing this the wave explodes when you look to hard shove it. You can also perma proxy and force him to sit under turret catching farm, and then you can get stuff like Voidgrubs, or counter jungling.

Boring matchup, all she will do is press E to farm and poke and will not go in until you are low. With your lifesteal you won't really be low so she won't engage unless someone else is there with her. She can use her ult to escape yours, but you can just slowly chip her down and then just dive her or force her to recall.

He is incredibly annoying and hard to catch, especially if the guy takes Phase Rush. Level 1 you want to walk with your wave so he cannot proxy early on and then get a free base. Just walk beside your wave so that if he wants to proxy he loses at least half his health. Even if you don't kill him that is enough, chunking him is very good as it means he can proxy for less time because he won't have the health to tank more waves. You can't really kill him because he will rush Boots of Swiftness, and if he has Phase Rush he really won't die. Your best bet is to do what he normally would, which is to just proxy like him, but this is better for you. Olaf is stronger on the all out 1v1 and can even take jungle camps. If Singed tried to get jungle camps he loses all his mana and half his health, and if the jungler comes to stop him, he is forced to execute. If the enemy jungler comes to stop you, then you probably just kill him and force more people to come deal with it. Singed does have better roaming than you, as he can fling people out of their turret and get kills, so you both have a way to get stuff after proxying. If you actually make Singed come try to stop you, then you are in a really good spot. It means he doesn't like going even with you and wants to put an end to it, but if you have Ravenous Hydra then you can just heal off the damage. In teamfights he can actually do a lot of work and you cannot chase him down because of his high speed, so your best bet is to ignore him and go into the backline.

Pre 6 he can actually keep you at bay decently due to the way he can kite you and cc you with his spells, but that's about it. After 6 you start to demolish him. You can kill him anytime your ult is up. Later on into the game it does becomes harder to 1v1 him. It's not like he will win the 1v1, but he will take about 10-15 seconds of sustained damage to kill him because he ends up being very tanky on health and armor. In teamfights you can just ignore him as he takes too long to kill and just rush his carries.
Once her spellshield is out she straight up dies, or she has to burn her Ghost or ult to survive. You don't even need to use yours, just burn them and go on her on the next all in.
He cannot pin you close to the turret nor can he drag you under the tower, so his only real way of winning lane is non existant to you.
Her speed is not enough to ignore your Q slow, so you can kill her anytime your ult is up.
If you hit Q on her she and she is not clue to turret you can ult her down and kill her. Usually in teamfights you want to kill her first as she giga heals everyone else.
If you tag him with Q he dies. He never wins the 1v1 against you. He cannot cc you with his E nor slow you with his W, so he just gets run over.
You beat him down in melee range and he cannot really escape you. In the hyper late game he does win the 1v1, but he shouldn't get there when you can either have a permanent freeze or just kill him.

Her range makes it very annoying to get close to her. If you can, look to proxy and keep her under turret permanently. It's actually better to not even interact with her at all as she will get passive stacks much, much slower. You can then look to get sutff on the map like Voidgrubs or invading the enemy jungler.

It's actually just a super annoying matchup. Not really hard, just very annoying. He can use his W to escape your ult, so you need to make sure that when you pop it you can guarantee the kill or you burn your ult and do not get the kill. His poke can be annoying, but he has no waveclear, meaning you can just go proxy and then look to roam, or counter jungle, or take Voidgrubs and he is stuck under turret. Even if you don't kill him you can have complete lane priority.
If you hit your Q on her she is forced to use her ult to get out or she dies.

Play it somewhat safe until Vampiric Scepter and the lane is over for him. Any short trade he does he loses because you can just regen right after. You can also keep him under his tower and never let him roam.
You can out 1v1 him in melee big time, even at 6. You just anihilate him.

He can actually fight you decently levels 1-5 and put a lot of pressure on you. If he actually has Phase Rush and goes Boots of Swiftness, then you're simply not killing him. He is too fast to do so. At that point you want to just try and set up a proxy and just permanently clear waves. This way he cannot poke you down or outrun you if you tag him with Q. You can also buy a Sweeper Lens and deal with his shrooms with it, or literally putting a control ward in the middle of the lane. If you hit him with Q and he has no Phase Rush you can run him down, but you need to hit every single Q. One missed Q means that you lose the kill and he can turn and kill you. In the mid game he can shroom up choke points and deal a ton of damage, do not underestimate how high his damage can get, it's quite absurd. You need to try and clear out as many shrooms as you can and ensure key chokes don't have any so you can safely walk around.
He cannot cc you, which is the way Thresh would win the lane, by pulling you close to the tower. Since he cannot do that he gets run over.

She can't really threaten to kill you. She can't even jump on you for a kill because you can just kill her yourself. It might be a bit hard to kill her because she can also jump away, but the cooldown is quite high and she has to play extremely safe until it's back up, and if you perma force her to use it then she will run out of mana.

You must respect his level 1, it is very strong. You will not win the all out fight at level 1. Starting level 2 you can fight him again, and it's even better levels 3-5. If you manage to get a kill during this time that is great, but if it's been going even you cannot go for a fight at level 6. If Trundle has Ghost+ Ignite he will destroy you, so you need to burn out the Ignite at the very least. If he doesn't have Ignite then you're fine. Another issue is that you can never let go of your lead once you get it. What I mean by this is that you have to always maximize everything during lane and never die. If the 2 of you just farm it out and he gets to Blade of the Ruined King, well you have just lost because you are never 1v1ning him again for the rest of the game. You need to abuse him like hell until his first item and never let you foot off his neck. You give him a single kill and you might not be able to 1v1 him for the rest of the game. He can also use his ult on you during teamfights and make you very squishy when you go in. His split push power is also massive, so you are forced to sit on the side lane for most of the game. Even if he is weak and has dies a lot of times, if you see he has Trinity Force or Hullbreaker you must stay on the side lane because in the span of about 20 seconds or less he can straight up end the game if he is at the inhibitor turret.

The issue with this matchup is that his ult directly counters your. It doesn't matter how much damage you deal because his ult makes him unable to die, so he can keep pushing damage into you and getting you lower while he basically stays the same health the whole time. If you go into an auto attack fight in melee range and try to resist until his ultimate is up, you will most likely die. This is why I like to take Ghiost+ Exhaust vs him. That way I can win the 1v1 in melee because of the high damage reduction. His ultimate also has a longer cooldown than yours so if he burns it you have about 30 seconds to absuse him with your ult while his is down. You can also basically never run as he can save his spin and chase you when you run, same with his W slow. You will get crushed in the 1v1 later on so you really need to take 1v1 fights when you have your Exhaust up and ensure you are able to win.
His gold card cannot stun you so if you hit a Q on him he dies or he is forced to use his ult to escape, since you have no cc to stop it.
You hit him with your Q he dies. The only time he doesn't is if he has his Q to stealth up, but anytime it's not up he dies.

If he is playing AD Udyr it's easy to beat him. He becomes harder to fight when he starts to get items as he will have high damage, but his reliability early on is much less. AP Udyr is where you need to be careful. He can fight you pre level 6 and put up a good fight. He is really annoying to deal with due to his constant healing and shielding. After level 6 it gets better, but generaly Udyr will also run Ghost and might go Boots of Swiftness, meaning it won't be super easy to keep up with him. There is also the issue of his tankiness. If he uses empowered W it can take you so much time to kill him that he can get to the safety of the turret and still have about 30% of his health left if he was full. He is incredibly tanky early on and usually hard buys tank items. He will be able to stonewall you in the side lane big time, so it's best to just look to group up with your team and take objectives or go into big teamfights where he is not as useful as you are.

Normally I would put this as an easy matchup before you ignore both his ultimate and his E fling so it shouldn't be super hard, but he can actually fight you really well. In this matchup Urgot typically takes Fleet Footwork, making it quite hard to catch up to him as reliably. However, if he does not have Fleet Footwork then yes the matchup is actually quite easy as he has no way to sustain himself or use an extra speedup to live. Levels 1-5 he can put up very good damage and even threaten to kill if you are not being careful, especially if he has Ignite. After level 6 he can keep his distance and farm from a semi safe distance. What you need to do is hold a freeze at all times and never let him farm up. With Fleet Footwork the only way you are ever killing him is if the wave is right at your tower and you chase him down with Ghost the entire way down, or else he lives, so having a solid freeze is key here. Another thing is that his first item spike is actually quite good. He can proc multiple Hullbreaker procs and ensure his dps is solid. He still has a hard time outright 1v1ing you, but you cannot ignore him damage, as a full rotation on all of his legs means you will lose a ton of health, more than you would expect.

He can beat you in the 1v1 in melee range due to the fact that most of the time they end up taking Barrier or Exhaust so this is why it's so tough. You might be able to beat him pre 6 but even that can be hard as you are going to get hit by his Q every single time, and he also has a heal cut zone in his kit. He has extremely high burst and it does not matter as much that you can walk through his ult. You must hard burst him and try to kill him as quickly as possible. This is why I really like Exhaust into him, so you can win those early 1v1s and get a lead going. Once you end up getting a lead it becomes much easier, but without that first one it's extremely tough. You can also just farm up until 2 items, but has very good lane priority until then.

She will destroy you. You are never EVER killing her. You have a window before 6, but that only happens if she doesn't have Ghost. If she does you do not have a single window where you can 1v1 her. She beats you every single time no matter what you do. It is living hell. Ask the jungler for help and pray he listens, but that's it. You will get absolutely destroyed in and out of lane. Your best bet by far is to try and force teamfights where you can kill her team quickly. If you want you can also take Ghost+ Teleport in your summoner spell choice because it is more reliable overall and gives you the ability to come back to lane quicker.
You can just walk through his cage and anihilate him.

He can actually kee his distance again you rather well and ensure he goes at least even vs you, which is a win for him. You can always look to proxy and then get something else on the map, like Voidgrubs or jungle camps, but you will probably not kill him if he permanently stays at full range, especially if he ends up running Phase Rush.
She cannot fear you and she basically has no mobility so you can walk all over her.
You beat her at every stage of the game, she can never beat you in the 1v1.
He is always forced to use his ultimate to escape as he cannot 1v1 you.

If he has Phase Rush it goes from easy to skilled, but it's still a decent matchup for you. If you tag him with Q he is dead almost every time as he cannot stop your engage at all. His initial burst damage should never be enough to outright kill you.

He will hard outscale you going into the mid and late game so you need to push him early on. The issue is, it's very hard to do so. If he has Phase Rush you are not killing him, he will be too quick. He also tends to run Ghost so it's even worse for you. Your best bet is to set up a freeze and try to deny as much farm as you can. Vladimir must walk up to last hit, he doesn't have any long range spells aside from his ultimate, so you can just sit back and freeze up and deny waves. Do not get baited trying to fight him or chase him down for a kill, all it will do is most likely break the freeze with you not being able to kill him as his speed combined with the safety of his W ensures he shouldn't die.

A lot of Volibears will play the setup with Unending Despair and Winter's Approach. If they actually end up doing this setup the matchup can be quite easy, reason being that he will never have the damage to kill you. He might heal a lot, but his overall dps is not enough to threaten you. He will be forced to use his ultimate to escape from yours, and because of how long of a cooldown it has on it, it's not worth it for him as it means your will always be up faster. Even if he has some ability haste at best it is 20 seconds longer than yours, which still means you are winning the ult trade. In the late game if he has that build you will mop the floor with him in side lanes as he will never do anything to you. You can also just ignore him and rush for the carries.

You absolutely destroy him. He cannot ult you and his fear is useless, and those are usually the tools Warwick uses to win a lot of 1v1 fights. On top of that, his W attack speed only happens when you are below half health, and if you instantly pop your ultimate at the start of a fight he is never gonna get you below half. The only thing you need to respect is his pre 6, as he can put up a very good fight, and that is the only time he can look to kill you, so just play it slow. Even if you miss some cs it's fine, just get the xp and you're fine.

His passive makes it really hard to beat him early on as he gets a ton of armor and health regen from it so you actually need to respect it. His level 6 is also quite powerful with how well he can all in. Short trades are fine, but they are better for him as he can burst you down quicker than you can burst him down. Ideally you try to play safe and slow until your first item, because once you get Sundered Sky the lane swings. The health gain is really good for Olaf, but more importantly, you can get a second Sundered Sky proc off of his clone, so if he ever uses his W you can get another 6% missing health proc. Olaf also has one of the highest base ad numbers in the game so even the flat heal is quite good on him, making it even better. Later on he will outvalue you most of the time in teamfights because of his ult having the ability to knock up twice, but you can also dive his backline or help kill him when he goes in. In the side lane it becomes quite close in the 1v1, but you should be able to win it as long as you can hit his clone for the second Sundered Sky proc, and if he uses his clone more than one time you will get even more procs for free.

Anytime you hit your Q on her she is basically dead, just know that her E damage is quite high so try to be at least over 40% health when you g for an all in to make sure you don't die from the burst.

His long range is what makes him annoying, like Hwei. However, unlike Hwei he cannot speed himself up when you try to fight him, and he is forced to slow himself down when he charges his Q, meaning it's much easier to hit him with your own Q and kill him.
Levels 1-5 he is decently strong, but you can still win it. After 6 you completely destroy him.

The only hard part is the fact that he can dash through minions and can make it to where your ult runs out, but that's it. Most of the time however, you don't even need to pop ult. Just walk up and start using auto attacks and E. And you will win the trade. You can also perma proxy, and if he tries to contest you then you can just kill him because there would be no minions to dash through.

This is a skill matchup but tends to be quite hard most of the time. It's on the very edge of being put as hard. In the early game it's mostly fine, it actually is a skill matchup. Yone can use his E to stall out your ult, or even trade ults, Olaf can stand in front of his ult to not let him escape,  Yone can use his Q to try to run, Olaf can hit Q reliably because he goes in a straight line, there's quite a good deal of things both sides can do and it comes down to mechanics and spacing. The issue comes after 2 items, where Yone completely anihilates Olaf in basically every single short trade. He can use his E at a safe distance and then walk up and start using his spells as normal, but Olaf can never use his ultimate in that fight because Yone can instantly snap back when he uses it, and Olaf has to distance himself until his E ends, and he is forced to do this every single time Yone uses E.He could also do that earlier on, but the problem is he can get punished for that normally because he wouldn't be using his E properly and could get punished in that downtime during laning phase. Outside of lane it can be close to impossible to win it, which is why I think this 3 core setup is best to be able to win this interaction out, because if he hard chunks you he can then use his ult to close the gap and kill you. The more items he gets the more unwinnable the 1v1 gets. At full build there's no world where you win it, so you need to win before that happens.

It can actually be kind of annoying with his constant poke. A lot of Yorick players will play a very poke heavy style, using E to just constantly send ghouls on you and chip your health down. His level 6 power is also decent. With his R up he can put up a good fight, and with Ignite he can even look for a kill. Your best bet to just just sustain up and not get greedy. Play it slow, even if he constantly sends his E on you, just hit his ghouls and keep lifestealing. With Vampiric Scepter the ghouls actually become a good source of gold. If he has his Miaden up he will constantly have the maximum of 4 ghouls, and if he sends them as much as possible with his E you can usually kill up to 16 of them in a minute or so, meaning it's 32 gold and you can just generate a gold lead off of constantly killing his ghouls. Later on all he will do is just split push a lot so you will be forced to match him or he will take your whole base, and could even end by himself. It sucks, but you need to deal with him. Alternatively, you can try to group up for teamfights and force a 4v5 quickly and look to end it before he has the chance to get a lot out of his split push.
Really not much to say here, you just anihilate her. If she roams you take all the plates and gain a massive lead.

His level 6 is actually incredibly strong. He can both heal and damage very well. It's also quite difficult to kill him as he can just use his E to escape after you pop your ult. Your best bet it try to win the sustain fight, doing very short trades and slowly chunking him down. Once you get Ravenous Hydra your lane is completely fine and it becomes very hard for him to win the trades. In the late game he cannot cc you down at all, so you can just rush his carries and he cannot stop you. He can still do good damage, but his cc does not matter as it does not affect you.

He doesn't really lane, and what I mean by that is he just perma waveclears and doesn't really interact with you. He will slowly poke you with his combo and then go for the kill. You cannot do much about this. Your best bet is, like in other matchups, to just try to proxy waves and then get someething else on the map, like stealing jungle camps or getting Voidgrubs. You don't do a single thing to him in the late game. He is hper mobile and you cannot catch up to him, ever.

She can always keep her dash to go over a wall, and that means you cannot just straight up ult her. On top of that, she can always trade ults with you and then even run you down if she has Ghost. You need to burn out her E before you ever think of going for an all in, and then look for it. Ideallt you instanty pop your Ghost and rush her down or you can end up not getting the kill or even dying.

He has super long range to poke from and perma spams abilities. Even if you hit Q on him he can use his W to put even more distance from you. You need to proxy waves and look to get something else on the map, like roaming or getting Voidgrubs.

His revive is super annoying. He also scales a lot harder than you in the late game. It's basically impossible to kill him. You want to proxy and then look to get something else on the map, like invading or getting Voidgrubs. He is actually super annoying to deal with. The reason the lane is hard is not because the champ itself can beat you in lane, but he can hyper stonewall you, and then also perma clears waves in the side lane with his double Q.
Her sleep does not affect you so you run her down once you tag her with Q.
Since she cannot root you, you can run her over once you hit Q.
